div.head: I Cn 14.2
div.ab: ⁊ healde man ælces Sunnandæges freolsunge fram Saternesdæges none oð Monandæges lihtingce ⁊ ælcne oðerne mæssedæg swa he beboden beo.
ælces Sunnandæges freolsunga fram Sæternesdæges none oð Monandæges lihtinge ⁊ ælcne oþerne mæssedæg, swa he bebodan beo.
in feriatione diei Dominicę ab hora nona Sabbati adusque diluculum secundę ferię et in sanctorum omnium sollempnitatibus, sicut a sacerdote fuerint nuntiatę.
⁊ healde man ælces Sunnandæges freolsunge fram Sæternesdæges none oð Monandæges lihtingce ⁊ ælcne oðerne [B is used for remainder of I Cn from this point.] mæssedæg swa he beboden beo.
And healde man ælces Sunnandæges freolsunge fram Sæternesdæges none oð Monandæges lihtingce, and ælcne oðerne mæssedæg, swa he beboden beo.
And the festival of every Sunday shall be observed from noon on Saturday till dawn on Monday, and every other feast-day as has been prescribed.
And each Sunday holy day is to be observed from midafternoon on Saturday until dawn on Monday, and every other feast day just as is ordained for it.
Und man halte die Feier jedes Sonntags vom Mittag des Sonnabends bis zum Morgenroth des Montags und jedes andere Kirchenfest, wie es geboten ist.
And let the festival of every Sunday be kept from Saturday noon until Monday dawn, and every other mass-day, as it is commanded.

div.note: Here B (CCCC 383 f. 43, c. 1125) begins in the old hand; the quire with I Cn 1–14.2 is torn out (pp. 42c–o hold a 16th-c. copy from A). Liebermann compares II Eg 5.; Robertson (p. 139) takes I Cn from B, which begins at ‘mæssedæg’ in 14.2, the earlier clauses being supplied from G
